body: Nightly batch jobs began finishing two hours later than usual after a configuration change, and the extended runtime raised monthly compute cost noticeably. Investigation showed the jobs were running on oversized general-purpose instances chosen years earlier for a much larger dataset. Moving the batch tier to compute-optimized instances restored the original runtime and removed most of the spike. The ticket recommends a quarterly review of batch instance families because dataset shape changes faster than instance choices.
title: Unexpected cost spike from nightly batch jobs

body: A storage audit found dozens of unattached volumes left behind by terminated instances, some older than a year. The volumes were small individually but added up to a meaningful monthly charge that nobody owned. The audit recommends tagging every volume with an owner at creation time and automatically reporting volumes that stay unattached for more than seven days. Deleting confirmed orphans required owner approval, which took two weeks for volumes whose owners had left the team.
title: Orphaned storage volumes found during audit

body: Password reset requests are the largest single category in the support queue this quarter, ahead of billing questions. Agents report that most reset tickets come from customers who could not find the self-service reset flow from the sign-in page. The ticket proposes moving the reset link above the fold and adding a guided reset article to the help center. A similar change on a sister product reportedly cut reset tickets substantially within one release cycle.
title: Password reset requests dominate ticket queue

body: The checkout service exhausted its quarterly error budget with three weeks left in the quarter after two overlapping incidents. The reliability team requested a freeze on non-essential changes until the budget recovers. Engineering leadership approved the freeze but exempted security patches and the already-scheduled cost optimization work on non-critical paths. The ticket notes that both incidents traced back to configuration changes that skipped the usual staged rollout.
title: Change freeze requested after error budget exhaustion

body: Late shipments this month concentrated on orders containing one component from a single supplier whose lead times doubled without notice. Planners increased safety stock for that component and opened a qualification process for a second source. The ticket observes that the supplier portal showed the delay two weeks before it affected shipments, but nobody was monitoring the portal feed. An automated lead time alert is proposed so planners see slippage when it starts, not when stock runs out.
title: Late shipments traced to a single supplier

body: Log ingestion charges doubled in the month after a major release because a new service shipped with debug logging enabled at full volume. The service owner had no dashboard for ingestion cost, so the increase was discovered by finance during month-end close. The ticket recommends per-service ingestion budgets with alerts at 80 percent of budget, plus a release checklist item that verifies production log levels. Sampling the noisiest informational stream is expected to recover most of the increase.
title: Log ingestion bill doubled after release
